provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Names a cause the speaker credits for a welcome outcome: the main clause reports something good the cause made possible (先輩が手伝ってくれたおかげで間に合った). Its siblings assign the cause differently: せいで blames it for an unwelcome result, せいか offers it as a guess. A noun attaches through の (眼鏡のおかげで). Used ironically on bad outcomes (おかげでひどい目にあった), the sarcasm works because the positive reading is the default.

examples.ruby: 先輩[せんぱい]が手伝[てつだ]ってくれたおかげで、締[し]め切[き]りに間[ま]に合[あ]った。
examples.english: Thanks to my senior pitching in, I made the deadline.

examples.ruby: 散歩[さんぽ]を続[つづ]けているおかげで、去年[きょねん]より体調[たいちょう]がいい。
examples.english: Thanks to keeping up my walks, I'm in better shape than I was last year.

examples.ruby: 新[あたら]しい眼鏡[めがね]のおかげで、細[こま]かい字[じ]がよく見[み]える。
examples.english: Thanks to my new glasses, I can read the fine print easily.

patterns.usage_note: Names a cause blamed for an unwelcome result: what follows せいで is damage, failure, or inconvenience (大雪のせいで電車が止まっている). おかげで is the positive counterpart, crediting a cause for a good outcome, and せいか marks a cause the speaker is only guessing at. A noun attaches through の, and せいでの stands before a noun (大雪のせいでの遅延).

examples.ruby: 寝坊[ねぼう]したせいで、面接[めんせつ]に遅刻[ちこく]してしまった。
examples.english: Because I overslept, I turned up late to the interview.

examples.ruby: 工事[こうじ]の音[おと]がうるさいせいで、少[すこ]しも集中[しゅうちゅう]できない。
examples.english: The construction noise is loud, and because of it I can't concentrate at all.

examples.ruby: 大雪[おおゆき]のせいで、電車[でんしゃ]が三時間[さんじかん]も止[と]まっている。
examples.english: Because of the heavy snow, the trains have been stopped for three hours.

patterns.usage_note: Offers a cause the speaker is not sure of: せい plus the uncertainty particle か guesses at what explains the situation (連休明けのせいか教室が静かだ). せいで states the cause outright and blames it for a bad result; おかげで credits it for a good one. Because the cause is only a guess, せいか also occurs with neutral or favourable results, though せい still tilts toward something unwelcome or odd.

examples.ruby: 連休[れんきゅう]明[あ]けのせいか、教室[きょうしつ]がやけに静[しず]かだ。
examples.english: Maybe because the long weekend just ended, the classroom is oddly quiet.

examples.ruby: 雨[あめ]が続[つづ]いているせいか、今年[ことし]の野菜[やさい]は値段[ねだん]が高[たか]い。
examples.english: Perhaps because of all this rain, vegetables are expensive this year.

examples.ruby: 昨夜[さくや]よく眠[ねむ]れなかったせいか、今日[きょう]は妙[みょう]に頭[あたま]が重[おも]い。
examples.english: Maybe because I slept badly last night, my head feels strangely heavy today.
